newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African textile merger gets preliminary approval.
newsitem.headline: S.African textile merger gets preliminary approval.

text.p: South Africa's Competition Board said on Friday it had given preliminary clearance to Consolidated Frame Textiles Ltd's (Confram) planned acquisition of textile firm Romatex Ltd.
The Board said in a statement the acquisition would not restrict competition in most of the markets in which the two companies operated as no overlap of operations existed.

However, within the markets of cotton-based woven fabrics and bed linen, in which both Romatex and Confram operate, the post-acqusition market share of the combined company would be 18 and 25 percent respectively in the two markets.

"(But) given the peculiarities of the textile industry and the substantial levels of imported products in those markets, these figures do not give rise to competition policy concerns that would warrant a formal investigation by the Board," it said.

The Board said in view of the comparatively short period given to it to evaluate the transaction, it reserved the right to review the preliminary clearance it had given should further information justifying such action be forthcoming.
Romatex chairman Brian Connellan on Thursday told Reuters the sale of his company to Confram would go ahead subject to approval from the Competition Board.
Romatex shares have been on a rollercoaster ride this week on reports the firm is to be sold to Confram, South Africa's largest textile company.

Shares earlier in the week surged on news of the planned sale, but on Thursday dived as much as 40 percent to an intraday low of 330 cents after Romatex said any bid for it would be at less than 330 cents a share.
Stocks were last trading at 330 cents, 40 cents or 11 percent weaker from Thursday's closing level of 370 cents.
